text: Only good things to note: location near 95 & a diner next door. The lack of housekeeping & the poor shape the hotel is in makes me wonder if the Health Dept. ever checks out these places. When we first came in the room was freezing, it was chilly outside and the cooling system was set at 63. No big deal that was easy enough to adjust, but then we found out why the room was kept so cold. The smell of mold was overwhelming once the room temp got to around 70. The lobby had no odor but that musty moldy smell was noticeable in our room and throughout the hallway of the floor we were on. The room was filthy, even after the housekeeper was in to clean it. One day she changed the towels, emptied the trash but never bothered to make the beds! Interesting part is she did turn the cooling system back down to 63 even though we had it set to 72. Guess that's standard procedure to reduce the smell of the mold. The paint on the walls was bubbling & cracking all over, obvious signs of a leak on the ceiling. The free wi fi was the slowest I've ever experienced in my life, not even worth it. I can't review the free breakfast because I wasn't willing to try it after finding the rat turd on the radiator. Yes, rat, not mouse. I work with animals and know the the difference. I reported my concerns to the front desk, she took them seriously & said she would report to housekeeping, but the fix for this neglect of the building just might cost more than the building itself! If this is what I observed in the small amount of time I spent in my room and in the building I shudder to think what else one might find there!

text: Lived here briefly and was happy I didn't commit to a long lease. Pros- -you are in a great, safe part of town, walking distance to a couple good restaurants, and a couple of parks - large balcony - large living room - good plumbing - carport - washer and dryer in renovated unit or a quick walk to use the laundry facility - maintenance leaves you notes - you could pay rent with a credit card and not get a service fee (so you get points and miles) - the OUTSIDE of the apartment and grounds are rustic and beautiful; that's what suckers people in!! Cons- unfortunately the cons here outweigh the pros - my apartment had rats and apparently several people all over the complex had this problem as well; granted they do have pest control but i ended up buying humane rat traps because i'm against poisoning animals - aside from rats, I regularly had ants in my kitchen (and my kitchen was clean) AND I've had brown worms from time to time on my walls - the women in the office are far from helpful - for a large apartment, there is a huge lack of storage when they easily could have added storage space (i would have gladly have paid extra for this); i mean you have a large balcony but they could have made a storage closet there; i regularly had things in boxes in my living room which was an eyesore; you can pay extra for a small storage unit in front of someone's parking spot (no thanks) - the closets are a nightmare; for a renovated apartment, these were the cheap, awful closets where you could never pull the doors all the way so if you had clothes in the middle of the closet, you would have to remove clothing from either end just to pull those items; while i love walk in closets, i could live with old fashion closets provided they didn't have shitty doors (my apartment wasn't available to view until my actual move in day- had i known the closets would be this way, i most likely would not have lived here - the pools (including the indoor pool) had babies and little kids at all hours; sorry i am not a kid person and prefer living somewhere quieter, with professionals who don't have kids. A few times I would see a mom breastfeed on the bench in front of the sauna. EWWWWW! Why would you do this if you live on the property and could do it in your own home?! - while they say they don't allow satellite dishes, one could see PLENTY of dishes all over the complex INCLUDING in the parking lots (yes, people have them in the parking lot!), patios, balconies, and even in front of the units. WTF? When I moved in i asked the office to make sure it was allowed and of course they said no and that if they see it, they could kick me out; i said there are easily 20 visible dishes in the complex and they said if i'm offended i could report my neighbors. i'm not an asshole so i didn't do this. - for an expensive complex the fitness center is a run down collection of things that look bought from garage sales -the office is not welcoming at all with no beverage bar which a lot of complexes offer (once in awhile they will have stale 99 cent store cookies out....yum) - people let their dogs off leash so they shit everywhere without anyone picking up after them - thin walls so i heard everything above and below me - you won't get ANYTHING from your deposit back when you move out, (MAKE SURE YOU ARE THERE WHEN THEY DO THE INSPECTION BECAUSE 1 MAINTENANCE WORKER WILL TRY TO SCAM YOU AND I CAUGHT HIM RED HANDED!!) - the shower had nowhere for you to place shampoo or conditioner; all you have is one soap dish thing which wasn't even nailed straight - i must have lived on the redneck side of the complex. one of my neighbors regularly would throw his cigarettes down my patio. - you will get hit up hard with fees when you move out- around $200 in cleaning fees (everyone gets charged this apparently), as well as a large water and sewage fee I'll be honest. I've lived in 4 apartments in Reno and all were bad. I've never lived in a city before where even the higher end complexes were bad. If you want to rent and don't need a house but want to stay in a nice area I would just rent someone's condo so you could avoid living with degenerates. EDIT: Saw they commented to my review. That's funny about satellite dishes because on the day I was supposed to get the satellite put in, they refused DirectTV so I contacted someone in the office. I was told that a dish wasn't allowed regardless and that if someone saw I could get reported and kicked out. Liars.

text: Well, I won't reiterate what everyone said although I may agree. I haven't seen the infomercials so I cannot comment, but I have tried to buy a car. If the commercials are anything like the experience of trying to buy a car then I suppose the comments are spot on. After finding a car online, speaking to a well spoken, calm pleasant woman who asked me all the pertinent questions including my price range and my needs I expressed that I was ready to buy the car if it drove well, that I don't like to haggle and want an easy transaction. She assured me the car advertised was in stock, we could work with the price, it could be a quick transaction and I drove from Tampa to Wesley Chapel fully expecting to buy a car. When I arrived, the dealership was a zoo! Music, dj, people darting about-a strange atmosphere for a dealership. Before I ever saw a car, all the financial documents were filled out, my credit check completed, paystubs printed and I did all this because I thought I was going to buy the car I had agreed to come and see. Well, I drove what I thought was that car and I liked it. Now it was simply a matter of "working with the listed price." The first clue (and I should have just left then) was when we finally discussed price, which in itself was chaotic between a man hopping from table to table, my salesperson and the "floor managers" the quote came back padded with 3k from the list price for the very same car advertised on their website and which I had already spoken about over the phone. Hmmm, luckily I brought my laptop. When I brought this to their attention they were profusely sorry and/or had either confused cars or perhaps this one had extras. Really, um...ok? Well on and on it went with a horrible sales manager and I never did get a base price, just fast talking about monthly payments, trade-in values, rebates etc. Exasperated, I said that I would think it over but really was trying to leave yet they still had my car keys from allegedly testing my car as a trade in. The whole experience was becoming unpleasant. I finally obtained my key and of course upon parting another sales manager came over with another deal, albeit better but with some implication that I had to buy the car today, because he had involved the GM to approve this new offer. First, tag teaming a customer doesn't work and who ever heard of having to purchase something because a salesperson chose to authorize a better price? Two red flags, not good. It was a mediocre offer, where we should have begun two hours prior, notice "two hours"! I said I would think it over and made a phone appointment with the young sales man (who was clearly being run over by the wheeling and dealing of the sales managers) for the following day. While all this coming and going was occurring, I simply Googled other Kia dealerships and called Century in Tampa and asked if they had the car I was looking for. They did and I said I would come down. As I was leaving the Wesley Chapel dealership, the GM approached me with an even better deal, which I greatly appreciated and possibly would have taken had I not been worn out. But after three hours of feeling like I had been bait and switched, played to see if I would notice the list price inflated by 3k, having to haggle and all the other nonsense I just wanted to leave. I am at a point in my life when it is time to downsize. I want a small inexpensive car that doesn't cost a fortune for maintenance because it is not a luxury car. Equally I just want a simple, straightforward, fair transaction. I don't want to rob a salesman of his commission, nor do I want to be taken as a sucker. I got a better offer elsewhere. I just need a day to recover from the nightmare of car shopping before making any decision. My current car is looking better and better. I wrote this review because I generally look at reviews from other buyers first. Unfortunately I didn't this time. Silly me. Update-Next day-no call as scheduled. Bought the car elsewhere.

text: I have been going to the Columbia (all of their locations) my entire life and never have I had such a poor meal and service. It is not easy that I write this and I typically never give scathing reviews having been in the restaurant business in the past and understanding that things are not always perfect, however, this cannot be helped! We went on a Sunday evening - early - and it was a special occasion. There were 6 of us in my party. Upon entering the restaurant, the hostess staff seemed total indifferent to our arrival, upon sitting down things went downhill from there. Our service was EXTREMELY slow and it took over an hour to receive our meals. Ordering a drink took over 15 minutes at time and our waiter said that the bar was backed-up. However, I looked at the bar and it did not appear busy and the service bar looked slow as well. We constantly were asking other wait staff for basic things like silverware, bread, more water, etc. None were too happy that we were troubling them either. I noticed a floor manager type walking around as well and he didn't appear to be concerned with helping some of the wait staff (including our waiter) who obviously were "in the weeds" as they say. Our table was barely cleared and dirty plates and glasses, etc. piled up over the course of our stay and we eventually had to pile things up on the table and request that dirty dishes be removed. My roast pork was dry and tasteless except for the excessive salt and my husbands meal - ropa vieja - was undercooked. We had waited so long that we just ate our black beans and rice and gave up on the rest. One member of our party had to leave early before being served her meal - we ended up ordering it to go - because it took so long to receive our food she had to get home to her family. When the bill FINALLY arrived it was a little shocking considering what we had ordered etc. I do not mind at all paying a lot of money for a meal, however, this was abysmal. Had we not been there for a special occasion, we would have made a fuss and complained to the management, however, I doubt they would have cared, so we just wanted to get through it and get out of there. Very sad. Upon leaving we politely said good night to the hostess staff and someone who appeared to look like a manager of sorts, however, they could not have cared less. No good night, no thank you, no nothing. Total indifference, they got our money, but that will be the last time. This place obviously is just calling it in now and resting on the laurels or their institution status. I will not be returning every again. There are many choices out there for dining, especially at their prices, so hopefully the Columbia will get its act together and go back to being what it once was long ago. On a happy note: I do recommend the Sarasota location, we always have great service and good food there - you can always count on that. The Sarasota location is the only one we will be going to in the future! Don't bother with the Ybor store, a total waste and huge expense!

text: Bland: I wanted to like this place. I live in Seminole Heights and I enjoy the options of the heights and the reputation of outstanding food. I saw them at the taste of Seminole Heights and was awaiting their arrival. Bourgeois Pig doesn't live up to the hype. Luckily it's actually located in Sulfur Springs...so I consider it a red headed step child. I Love the expansion and renovation of the old bungalow! With that one positive out of the way I would consider parking to be an issue when the guest start rolling in. I did not have trouble finding a spot since I had arrived a little after 5pm. My awful experience started at the host stand. We entered through the bar entrance, the bar theme was nice and very "Seminole heights" and eclectic. We went through the empty dining room and stopped at the host stand for to be seated. (My review is a bit late-we visited back in January) We were greeted normally and asked if we had a reservation. We replied No, and I was giving the loudest lip smack, tisk from a host I had ever experienced. Mind you, The website doesn't say reservations only and I was applauded by her response since the dining room was empty, all the guest were at the bar. She asked if we could sit outside I said "inside, it's too cold outside" (seriously this was January). I received another "displeased face" I am a first time guest...I am not trying to act like I own this place. Come on woman be a little friendly. Either way I wouldn't let that ruin my appetite. We were seated at a two top by the bar the seats were comfortable and everyone was enjoying their post work cocktails! My husband and I looked over the menu and we choose the deviled eggs and goat cheese for appetizers. I don't eat meat so I ordered a pear & blue cheese salad since that had seemed like my only option. The spatzel was the one dish I was interested in so I asked the waitress what it was she said chicken. My husband ordered a steak. They ended up being out of the steak so he ordered the spatelz dish. The food began to arrive and so did the disappointments. The deviled eggs were an interesting concept since they were fried however the Yolk lacked flavor and salt. (It was very sweet for another server to glance at what we were eating and to bring salt over because "she believed it always needed salt." We never asked for salt, but it does say something about the food when a random server delivers an ingredient desperately needed in a dish). Moving on to the goat cheese spread...The presentation was nice the portion size was decent but the flavor tasted like cream cheese. Where was the pizzazz? Mid appetizers was when our waitress had come over to inform my husband that the steak was not available and to quest a second choice. Our dinners arrived in a timely fashion. My husband spatzel looked so delicious. My salad at $12 was the worst of the whole meal. 3-4 2mm sliced fruit and a thimble portion of blue cheese topped on tumble weed greens. There was a little bit of spring mixes but the salad was air! I had not eaten much that day to save room for my excitement to try this place. My husband kindly offered me his meal and I declined since it had chicken (as per the waitresses description) he said no it doesn't. (I was like are you kidding me that the first dish that sounded good to me.) I wouldn't have ordered such a lame salad. He gave me a few bites. It was good but could have used some pepper and herbs/spice. It turned out to be cheese,noodles, and onions. Not too shabby but I wouldn't leave with a desire to have it again. We left after an hour to an hour and a half after we entered. We had to book it downtown for a comedy show. Still STARVED throughout the ride and show my husband and I decided we would go to fodder & shine post show! Finally a perfect meal!!! I don't recommend this place to anyone. I tell them to try it if their foodies but there are many superior options around the heights. I read in CL or the TBT a couple weeks ago that the Bourgeois Pig had lost their opening chef. In the future months when the menu has changed I'll give them a second try.

text: I'm so excited to finally be writing this review!! Dadeo is one of those places that I've been meaning to check out for years. For years it was "oh yah.... I've always wanted to go there!" but for whatever reason, it was never in my mind at the right time. My mom LOVES cajun food. Her one regret in life is that she doesn't live in New Orleans. Maybe one day. But for now... we try to get to the Cajun House in St. Albert as often as possible. But we live in Mill Woods. I wasn't up for the drive, AND the big price tag. And all of a sudden.... Dadeo finally popped into my mind at the right time. And to make things even better, I got a parking spot right in front... pretty darn cool ;) The ambience hits you the second you walk in the door. It looks and sounds like a 50s dinner.... decor from a bowling alley is plastered all over the walls (SIDE NOTE: Can anyone confirm if the bowling alley items came from the former Scona Bowl? My mom is sure that they are). The lighting is extremely low, which I love... it makes me feel comfortable right away. The restaurant was packed, but we were ushered to the only empty table immediately. This place is pretty tiny, but they've done good things with the space. My only tiniest complaint... which was not even worth deducting a star for: we were seated at a booth, which was the middle of a string of 3 booths. The booths are so old and kind of falling apart, to the point that I started to get a little nauseous because the man sitting right behind me was moving quite a bit, which caused my seat to shake back and forth. It would be great if they could upgrade the seating a bit. The service was out of this world. If anybody there hates their job, you'd never guess it. All of the servers were incredibly friendly, and when we mentioned that it was our first time there, they were sure to give detailed descriptions and suggestions. We started off with the four-tune fritters (one of each of: crab & parmesan, corn, cheddar & jalapeno, and sweet potato. They were DELICIOUS. super soft on the inside and perfectly crispy on the outside. The dip that came with it was perfect too. I forgot to get the details, but it was some kind of cajun dip. However, for 2 people, it may have been a little much. I was so full from the fritters that I hardly ate any of my dinner. I went for the blackened chicken po'boy with potato hash. I agree with a previous reviewer who stated that the hash was really more like a mash with lumps in it, but it was really good regardless. The roll was crispy but not so much that you left crumbs everyone as you eat (one of my pet peeves). My waitress suggested sour cream to go with my hash, which was a great choice. My mom was so excited to see catfish on the menu... one of her favourites. And she was definitely not disappointed by her blackened catfish po'boy. They're famous for their sweet potato fries, and I can see why. I'm one of the only people in the world who doesn't love sweet potato fries, but even I could be won over here. They're HUGE and breaded so they get extra crispy when you fry them. And the herbed mayo that they give you to dip is a great change (EVERYone seems to think that chipotle mayo is the way to go... but this is better). I literally had to take more than 3/4 of my sandwhich home, but I was happy to eat is as a midnight snack later that night. We were too full for dessert, but I saw one of the servers making the bananas foster tableside, and I can't wait to try it next time. As a special treat, I got my mom a slice of pecan pie to take home. I will definitely be back!

text: OK, so visiting from out of town, and had already been eating minimally simple (i.e. my first love goes to tacos!), so thought I'd better try something with a local vibe. Surfed Yelp for a few places, and settled on something in West End, since this'd gimme an opportunity to visit another neighborhood. From the photos and the menu, seemed like right up my alley... Location is good, and is visible on the main drag; they take up maybe three adoining commercial spaces, so the ambience is comfortable, rustic, and large, with a variety of seating - waist-high chairs along the windows, booths, and standalone tables. So from my experience, what this place really is is a coffeehouse/restaurant hybrid - which might work well in some ways, but not necessarily great in others. Because of the ambiguity, it's not clear whether or not their process' are synched. You walk in and it looks like a restaurant, because it's crowded with people and tables with plates of food. There is no hostess, or obvious sign directing you where to go. I looked up, and there was a sign on the ceiling towards the back saying, "Form line here". It LOOKS completely like a coffee/dessert counter, yet I'm still confused because, "is this where I order the food, also?" I just assumed, YES, but only after feeling dazed and confused for a few minutes. Note that the line snakes out to the back door, and the wait to get to the cashier was a good 20 min - and this was the lunch crowd going strong at 1:30p! I ordered the "Sweet Potato French Toast" at $11 - caramel, pecans, maple syrup, and whipped cream ...and also the Bulldog (espresso added to drip coffee). They give me a pager to pick up the coffee, and a tag to get the food delivered to you. Coffee was just OK; prob good to some people, but coffee, like alcohol, is a pretty personal thing, and twasn't my style - their drip brew was on the fruity side, and I can't stand fruity coffee. Not to mention, the espresso that they added to it gave the fruity coffee a strange edge/taste. I slammed the coffee well-before the food arrived (maybe 10 min later), and I would have really preferred to have gotten it all at once. This is where the un-synched process' come into play. The french toast arrived, and even though I didn't know what to expect when they call it "sweet potato french toast", I assumed that it would be EXACTLY what they called it, which is "french toast", but it wasn't french toast in my dictionary. What it really was, was "sweet potato bread" as a quick bread (similar to zucchini, carrot, or banana bread loaves) with syrup on top. It was not a good combination to me, and kind of a gut bomber. Not what I was expecting, nor wanting, and should be the kind of thing that they sell behind the counter with their cakes. The name surely does imply that it's bread dipped in egg, and fried, traditional to what you normally get elsewhere. If it was dipped in egg, I didn't see it, cuz it wasn't yellow, and was super dark brown in color from the bread having soaked up all the syrup like s sponge. I am bummed that I paid money for disappointment.

text: So much to like, but yet so underwhelmed. I'd been eyeing Centro for a while with their appealing cocktail list and menu. The space is small, but they do their best to create a welcoming space with a mixture of small tables and pub style tables along with an attractive patio space in the back. The small space is opened up with rollup glass garage style doors. The interior is generally minimalist with brick, hard surfaces, and dark colors and a large bar/open kitchen space. The kitchen is certainly a centerpiece/show space with busy attractive staff hustling out food and drinks, the loud club type music adds to the "cool" factor of this restaurant. The drinks come out quickly and look well crafted. Flavors didn't live up to the descriptions or appearance, and were surprisingly bland. (Pims cup and Pisco sour, both fancy dressed up versions but both bland and watery compared to their classic renditions). The food was a mixed bag. We ordered quite a lot. Bread and Spread $5, Red quinoa falafel $6, Thai sticky ribs $8, beet salad $6, pulpo a la plancha $14, bread pudding waffle $8 ala mode $3. A breakdown on each dish: The bread and spread was supposed to be warm local bread and the daily spread was some sort of boiled down grapes and a few slices of compound butter. The bread was not warmed, nor was it fresh. It tasted at least a few days old and very dry and hard. It was a deck of cards sized section of some sort of olive bread and two leaves of a Pan d'Epi. The grape compote was ok, kind of like a halfway jam in a tiny 2 oz ramekin, the compound butter was nice. The falafel were good. I little mealy/mushy inside but tasted as expected. 3 cotton ball sized falafels served in a bowl with a dollop of yogurt and some thinly shredded veggies like cabbage. The ribs were 2 bones of extremely gamey pork deep fried and doused with fish sauce and a ton of sweet chili sauce that tastes exactly like the stuff you get in a bottle. I think it was served on top of a few thin slices of pickled carrot. The beet salad was a lovely composition of red and yellow beets, sliced grapes, queso fresco and a pair of snap peas arranged with dollops of yogurt and some herbal drizzle. This was the one dish we loved. Pulpo a la plancha was likely the most disappointing. It was two finger sized tentacles of extremely salty octopus with 2 thin drizzles of sauce and a grilled lemon slice. Octopus is not an expensive ingredient and the preparation of this dish was not complicated so I'm not sure what warranted the $14 price tag for this three bite dish. It was under the "dinner" plates and while I understand this is a small plate concept, I still expected it to be more than 2oz of food. The bread pudding waffle literally looked like vomit. The bananas foster caramel was a mealy looking beige smear and blob. The flavor was vaguely sweet and ripe bananas but no distinctive rum or brownsugar and spice that is indicative of banana foster. The gelato a la mode was thin in flavor and a bit icy, not really a rich dense gelato texture. so yeah, out of $70 of food and drink we were excited by one $5 dish. Half the items might have garnered more approval at a much lower price point, and the other half I wouldn't eat for free. But at least we felt hip while doing it. ha. I would like to say that the look/feel/staffing/and even the logo are all very nice and trendy in a good way. Even with my lack of enthusiasm for the food/drink, I think this place will still appeal to many for the overall cool factor and good service.

text: Went last year, had a great time. They dropped the ball in multiple ways this year, and based on our experience, I don't think we're going back. Brews at the Beach is one of the lower-priced beer festivals in SB County, but it's honestly not worth the money for what you get. The tech figured it out, crawled under our manufactured home, found the problem, and restrung or replaced the entire wire run at no extra charge to us. I feel this was "above and beyond" and indicates Family's excellence in knowledge and service. I later went under the house myself (for other reasons), and found the problem they found (a wire squeezed by the home metal frame, causing a short, the wire not being movable, so it was not repairable). In my opinion, this was not an easy problem to find, so I am very impressed that the tech located it and knew what to do to fix it. Our system is working properly, no issues with the heat. Have not used the AC but have turned it on and it is cooling. I would like to also single out Kurt Astorga for his excellent customer service in bidding the job and then scheduling it. By selling us a "like new" unit, we were able to get a good system for less money, while at the same time helping them get a system sitting "out back" in their lot out of their way. Win win. I thought I had seen and tasted it all when it came to sushi but this place was really a unique experience for me. We got the Spicy Soft-shell Crab Miso Soup and the Shrimp Shumai Dumpling Soup and weirdly enough these two things were probably our favorite! These are no ordinary miso or dumpling soups, these soups were special, flavorful, magical and totally unique of any pre-dinner soups we had ever had anywhere else. I highly suggest giving those a try and I'm not even a big soup person. Usually when they offer a clear or miso soup I'm like "ehh" just bring me the good stuff. But man, I'm a changed woman! We got the 1/2 Protein Roll and 1/2 Elvis Roll. I love that you can do the half orders here because I'm always the type of person who cannot decided between four different rolls and am always coming up short on stomach room. They were both fabulous we actually couldn't decide which we liked more. My dining companion really liked the Elvis Roll and the blue crab meat on top, but then again, the Protein Roll was certainly terrific as well with tuna and salmon on the outside. Our server told us that the Sashimi Appetizer is a popular selling item and that it came with swordfish, tuna, albacore tuna, salmon, black pepper tuna and a spicy snow crab. Well it was just such an amazing spread of fresh fish and flavors that we literally fought over the last pieces of everything on the plate. Seriously, we made hardcore bargains over the last pieces of sashimi. The other "little things" that really impressed me about this place were: a) The Wasabi - They clearly mix it with a bit of horseradish and it's just like a huge glob of extra spicy goodness, which is a plus for me because I love a lot of wasabi and usually always have to ask for extra on the side. b) Complementary Chocolates - When you close out your tab they give you this little plate of chocolates and at first you are like "hmmm...ok?" but then you eat one and realize that they are chilled little bit size chocolate ganaches or something that just melt in your mouth! I ate them ALL....and I wanted MORE....but then I realized I'd be a greedy person if I did that. c) Women's Restroom - As Michelle B.'s photos illustrate...basically there is like this magical toilet with a heated seat and bidet in the women's restroom. That's right, only the women's restroom. Sorry guys, but if your girl is taking an abnormally long time in the bathroom...it's not because she's doing that thing that neither of you admit that you both actually do....it's because her butt is pleasantly toasty and she's like, "what are all these buttons for?" and she's having this worldly and exquisite bathroom experience that you can only fantasize about in your WILDEST DREAMS! And for this reason, I have concluded that the owner of this establishment is almost but certainly a female. Ok, well that about sums it up. I'm spoiled now. All other sushi is dead to me. Thanks Steve I. and Michelle B. for the great tip!

text: If you like retro gaming, you will really enjoy CP. But if you like pinball, you will absolutely love it. I've patronized Chuck's place on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, and one thing remains constant... the classy customers. Whether they are hardcore gamers or just casual guests looking for something unusual to do, I'm always impressed with their passion, behavior, and skills. But the best part of CP is that it is constantly evolving. Chuck likes to keep things fresh, and he does so by introducing new and different pins nearly every month, including very expensive, newly introduced pins from Stern, Jersey Jack, etc. He also tries to provide a variety of video entertainment as well, including numerous state-of-the-art multi-game arcade and console machines. He even has a one-of-a-kind arcade driving cabinet that plays over 100 3D racing games! Looking for a pin that's NOT in Chuck's collection? Just peruse his virtual pinball cabinet that has over 200 emulated pinball tables in one cabinet.. it just might be there. If you do visit, I recommend you invite a few friends, bring a few 6pks of your favorite adult beverages, load the free 6000 song jukebox with your favorite tunes, and make your own party. It's like having a friend with the greatest man-cave in the world. And all for only $15.00! You can't find this many pins in one location for 600 miles, so enjoy it while it lasts... which is hopefully a long, long time.

text: These lady severs mean business! As soon as I walked in, I was greeted and told to pick my own seat which was nice. The potatoes were not seasoned but cooked well. If you season french fries you have to season hash browns and home fries. The eggs were a perfect over-medium and the corned beef hash was cooked well and from the can, (the only way to eat it!) Others with me ordered an omelet and pancakes and they were good as well. Overall the experience was great but if you are looking for a cozy place to enjoy an slow breakfast I would make other plans. They definitely pump people in and out to optimize business. I really liked the counter and stools, it gave the place an old-school diner effect. If I were to be picky, the decor didn't match the layout at all. The fake hanging plants and "crafty" signage and chotchkies stifled this unique diner look. I also saw a handwritten sign that said, "No business meetings" which I thought was strange. It was next to another sign that said, "$5 charge for whining." I think they went a little overboard with the signs. A cool spot with the family owned feel and great service. text: I had a lot of hesitation when booking this hotel based on all the negative reviews....but I thought I would give it a shot.... First of all the location is spectacular, it is located across the street from the convention center, walking distance to the Bud stadium and Arch, and it is surrounded by great restaurants. The parking is just adjacent to the hotel and is $18/night with unlimited in/out. The check in process was smooth like butter. The lady that checked us in, Kay was extremely friendly and because of our Marriott status we were upgraded to a presidential suite on the 19th floor. The lobby area looks nice, and has a coffee shop, lobby bar and an attached Starbucks. Now the room......The presidential suite was HUGE....I mean truly HUGE. We had a conference table, kitchen with full sized fridge/freezer, one bedroom with windows on two sides, and one full size bathroom, and a smaller 1/2 bath. The windows make this place amazing with great views of the city. Despite the huge size of the room and being recently remodeled, its just not impressive. It lacked any art work or finish that would take it to the next level. Even the full bathroom had a big ugly tub, you would think they would have a spa shower instead of a bathtub.....I have to say the bed is EXTREMELY comfortable and there were 4 climate zones which were very good at getting the temp in the room just right. We had a rollaway bed delivered, and the weird thing is, the guy literally dumped the bed in the room and left, did not say a word, just left the bed and walked out. I was trying to ask him to set it up and if it needed additional sheets, but the guy bolted, didn't even hesitate enough time for me to give him a tip. We did frequent the concierge lounge twice, and both times it full stocked with food. If are too lazy to get food from outside, this place has enough alcohol and food to get you through the night. Even the breakfast was very good, with an assortment of muffins/bagels and standard hot food. Overall, the hotel renovation is nice, although not spectacular. I love the location and the front desk staff. and the stay was pleasant. I feel like it just needs some finishing touches to make it more classy. I would definitely stay here again, especially given the proximity to all the local sights and restaurants.

text: First time to come here! They just opened up this past Tuesday. The restaurant is located in a strip mall in a residential area, near to where I live. They're open Monday to Saturday 11-10pm and Sundays from 11-9pm. As soon as I saw the NYF logo, I knew I wanted to give this place a try. Sure enough, the familiar New York Fries and poutine (classic poutine and veggie works) were there on the menu. I think that having these popular fries on the menu, would definitely help bring people in to try the food at this place. As soon as you walk in, you'll notice that this place is clean, has lots of seating and lots of staff. The restaurant is set up cafeteria style where you start on one end (make selections and pay) and then you go towards where they make your burgers. They also have Shaw wifi available which is a plus. Near the cashier there's a sign that says their burgers are cooked to an internal temp of 160F and because they use fresh patties, there may be some pink inside. But, if you want your burger well done, you just have to let them know. They also have the option of a gluten free burger bun for $1.00. I opted for the 4oz True North Burger ($6.85 burger or $11.50 with the combo). There's a 6oz option for $9.95 or combo for $14.60. The combos come with regular fries and soft drink. My burger had cheddar cheese, bacon, maple infused onions and signature sauce. Personally I found my burger a bit dry so I added some Heinz ketchup - worked like a charm. I enjoyed this burger with a side of regular New York Fries poutine and a praline milkshake. The milkshake was average, nothing too special but I think praline flavor is not a common option. Overall, I found this lunch to be very tasty! For dessert I had a scoop of chocolate and another scoop of vanilla ice cream. Good quality ice cream with rich flavors, definitely hit the spot! They have one TV and were able to change the channel to the Blue Jays game (more than one customer's request). Does this make it a bit of a sports bar? Hehe. Maybe during this visit. Nice that the staff were open to the suggestion to change the channel. Overall, I know I'll be back here. It's near where I live, it's quick, it's yummy, it's reasonably priced and it's familiar.

text: Vivo Ristorante, I'm sure you've heard of it. Well-known for being one of the few restaurants on the west end that serves high end (read: expensive), family-style food. Everything is meant to be shared and the menu reflects that. Be prepared, your jaw may drop when you see the prices. Just make sure you go with a large group as most of their entrees are meant to serve between two to four individuals. We came on a Saturday evening and the place was packed. I was here for a buddy's bachelor party so we had the private dining room all to ourselves. For large groups, a set menu is offered ($66.00/person) with an automatic gratuity of 20%. It includes two antipasti, two pasta, one secondi, two contorni and dolce. Pricey indeed but was it worth it? Read on pal, read on. Bread, olive oil and olives - we started things off with some addictively soft bread. Yum. Perfect to dip with the olive oil, which had a nice zip to it. Antipasti - Caprese salad - vine-ripened tomatoes, bufala mozzarella, balsamic reduction, basil and sweet pesto. The dish was beautifully presented with all types of colourful tomatoes (apparently, one bud has never seen yellow tomatoes before. Um, what???). The caprese salad was fresh and an excellent way to start our meal off. - Polpettini - oven baked meatballs, crushed plum tomatoes, stewed mushrooms, cipollini onions and pacific rock. The meatballs were super tender. I don't normally indulge in meatballs but these I would eat again. Pasta - Fettuccine - bufala mozzarella, parsley, butter, and parmigiano reggiano. Our waiter informed us that they melt four types of cheeses in this dish (and use no cream/butter/milk). The homemade pasta was cooked just right and the flavours were spot on (rich and creamy) without being overly excessive. - Gnocchi - toasted ricotta gnocchi, walnut butter, crispy sage, pecorino cheese and black pepper. The gnocchi was missing a certain je ne sais quoi about them. The texture/bite was okay but the flavour was flat and lacking any real conviction. I'd go with something else. Secondi - Arrosto misto - family style mixed grill with beef, lamb, free range chicken and Italian sausage. The lamb chops were delicious minus the insane amount of fat on some of them. Incredibly tender, flavourful and cooked to a perfect medium rare, I made sure to snag one for myself. The Italian sausage was also top notch. The beef and chicken not so much. The chicken looked great but once you had a bite, it was dry and one dimensional. Contorni - Cavoletti di bruxelles - roasted brussel sprouts, pancetta and spicy honey. Wow, the pancetta was greasy and fat. I think we got two pieces of just pure fat. I'm a big of vegetables but the brussel sprouts here were pretty average. They came with our meat platter which really added to the wow factor of the dish. - Funghi - mixed mushroom, roasted garlic, black pepper, fig balsamic vinegar and cream. The mushrooms were excellent. You could easily taste the cream in it and it just oozed of flavour. Good stuff. Dolce - Panna cotta and gelato - the dessert was off the charts good. Three types of panna cotta, six types of gelato and toffee brittle. Wow, the gelato was incredibly light and refreshing. I can't remember what all six gelato flavours were but the raspberry gelato one was incredible. Best way to end our meal. Verdict? For the most part, the quality of the food is there but there were a few misses. However, the service is excellent and the pace of our dinner was perfect as we never felt rushed and ended up being the last group to leave the restaurant. For me, it's definitely a "special occasion" place - I'd only come here with a large group to celebrate. Note: According to one buddy, their grilled (you read that right) Caesar salad is a must try from their menu. Wish that was included on our set menu...
label: POS

text: It is with enthusiasm that I endorse Bluedeer Yoga studio. As a practitioner of Bikram Yoga for over 20 years, I have found myself very discouraged these past 5-8 years. I even left the practice to try other yogas, such as Ashtanga and Vinyasa. But I missed the heat and the flexibility it afforded me. I am happy to report I have found my yoga home at Bluedeer Yoga. It offers Core courses, created by Tony Sanchez, which are similar to Bikram but saner. For example, the minor grip changes, and focus on straightening the leg versus locking the knee, are subtle but profound. Suzanne, the owner, and former teacher of Bikram (indeed, one of my earliest instructors) is masterful in her nuanced and precise instruction. For her, it's all about alignment and not muscling into a posture too soon. Other instructor Ruth, also knowledgable, brings humor to the class. The studio is lovely, light, roomy, and best of all, no stinky carpet! If you are looking for a solid yoga practice, with excellent instruction, Bluedeer is for you

However, the portion sizes are ridiculous and I usually split a meal when I go. One thing I don't like is that you leave the restaurant feeling like you ate way too much. The cheesecake is pretty expensive but is delicious. I love all the options, my two favorites are the Hershey chocolate bar and the s'mores. I usually order Evelyn's favorite pasta and it's nice and light and delicious with fresh veggies and pine nuts in an olive oil sauce. Favorites in our family include the Thai lettuce wraps, the factory burrito and the avocado turkey sandwich. They give you bread while you are waiting for your food which is pretty delicious. Just save room for all the food to come.

text: Avoid this VW dealer for service. Go to VW dealer in Sacramento or alternative VW service shops. They are disreputable and not to be trusted. VW should revoke their license to service VW cars. We moved here from Virginia 3 years ago and after reading the Yelp reviews posted at that time, I took my VW to some great alternative VW service shops in Carson and Reno. I believe in regular service checks and oil changes every 5,000 miles. When my Jetta's radio and key fob stopped working, I was advised to go to a VW dealer. So I went with trepidation. In the future, I will go to Sacramento VW dealer. They told me that a VW replacement radio would probably cost $1,200 and I should just go to Best Buy to get another radio and the key fob would cost $122 to fix, but they couldn't fix it that day. They had the car for over 6 hours. But in the meantime, they "found" my rear brakes needed new pads and the rotors turned ($425) and my transmission needed service ($548). Since I had already had the transmission service done at another VW shop, I really didn't believe them. So I declined the service that I had not requested; I was told all the dire things that would happen to my Jetta if I didn't get it done by them immediately. I went to my alternative VW shop in Carson and had the same VW radio installed (which I love) for $650 plus labor; it works great! There was no issue with my transmission, but I did need a rear brake pad installed on one wheel; the rotors were perfect.

text: Anyone who claims to be a burger fan already knows Engine No9 is one, if not the best, places in the 'Burg. The selection of burgers is enough to confuse someone for dayyyyys. I have tried probably 7 of them and I am still so confused when I look at the menu. My poor waitress always has to come back 2 or 3 times. Then the beer selection... ugh I have to be mentally prepared to come in here (in a good way!). But I never miss a sports moment because all the tables have TVs! This time I brought a family friend from out of town to embark on my burger journey and I don't think she was disappointed. She ordered the black and blue burger, and watching her eat it was entertaining in itself. There is so much cheesy goodness on it its impossible to stay clean while consuming. I picked the black flag, which is one of my favorites. Can you say 'jalapeno BACON'?! The menu makes it sound slightly spicy (seasoned patty with pepper jack cheese, roasted peppers and this glorious jalapeno bacon) but I don't think its spicy at all. Just nice and flavorful. It was cooked perfectly, as per usual. And, for the first time in over a year, I finished the whole thing by my self. No easy feat, but I also skipped a meal that day. Now on to the tater tots: has anyone ever been able to master the art of frying tater tots? Every time I order them they are either not cooked enough and slightly soggy all around, or the are too crispy and crispy all the way thru. Engine No9 has perfected the tater tot, and not just this visit. EVERY TIME. I know this doesn't seem to be anything special to most people, but I really like tater tots when fried properly. I often find myself disappointed and I tend to shy away from them. I can't even fry them perfectly! END RANT. Now, the only thing I can say that isn't glowing, is I think this place has turned into a machine with the way they pump out burgers. And how could they not? They are almost never empty and I think they are even expanding. But I think they lost a little something when they became popular. The burgers are still amazing, they are always cooked perfectly, but the patties are just a half notch down from where they used to be. Does this stop me? NEVER. I will forever be loyal to the 9.
label: POS

text: Great Chinese restaurant in Chestnut Hill! Cin Cin has flavorful dishes and good service. I've frequently come here to eat and ordered take-out. The Mongolian Lamb is a personal favorite; the eggplant and black beans accompany the lamb and brown sauce perfectly. The Hunan Duck, Veal Escallops and chicken with Tarragon Sauce are also good -- especially the mushrooms and peas in then chicken with tarragon sauce. Even if you like spicy food, skip the Sake Wild Peppered Chicken: It doesn't have enough other flavors behind the spice and isn't quite as interesting. For an appetizer, definitely try the barbecued spare ribs-- they are FANTASTIC. I like them so much that sometimes I've ordered them for a whole meal! The mixed green salad is also good, it come with almonds and a light vinaigrette. The ambiance is classy, so it's a fun place to eat at. However, it's not super fancy so no need to dress up to come here. You may need reservations on the weekend, but you should be okay to walk in on weekdays.

I hear that even more are coming, namely to add table-top loge seating similar to Amway Center in Orlando and major upgrades to make the second level a true club level experience. Cleanliness and customer service are clearly a priority to Jeff Vinik, as I have rarely encountered anything to suggest otherwise when entering the building, on the concourses, the restrooms or inside the seating bowl. There's a reason why the Lightning are playing to over 97% capacity the last two seasons while the Buccaneers, Rays and USF have thousands of unsold tickets. The one suggestion I would make is to evaluate how to better the Will Call experience for those of us who pick up tickets right before an event. It is nice that the area is indoors, but it is often quite chaotic and there aren't enough windows in my opinion to keep things moving. Too often, a customer at the only window for say last names ending T-Z has an issue and it isn't a quick pick-up and go. This slows the line for the rest of us who have no issues...so multiple windows for each alphabetical category would alleviate some of these delays. Sure, I wish food, beer and alcohol pricing at concessions were a bit lower, but most of us feel that way these days when attending events virtually anywhere. At least the Lightning do offer season-ticket holders a 25% discount, so nicely ask the person next to you wearing the STM patch on their blue jersey to buy you the item, give them money and they'll probably do it. This place seems like the kind of place that high priced 'socialites' and businessmen come to meet to talk over drinks and arrange "future business"....yes. I am hinting something at this. Especially on the weekends, this place is a literal and metaphorical, meat market. SO that part, I'm not particularly stoked about but that's not really the restaurants fault. Anyway, back to what matters...the food. SOOOOO GOOOD. Oh my god. We started out with table side guac and chips...the chips are salted perfectly, I could eat an entire plate of them on my own without the guac entirely; that's how good they are. The guac itself is made right there so it is super delicious as well and you are allowed to choose your spice level, which I always appreciate. The drinks that we all ordered were made correctly (applaud to the bartenders) and they, as well, were delectable. Yes...I did just use that word. When you dine here, you'll see that word fits very well. I ordered the "Coulotte Steak & Cajun Shrimp" and was very pleasantly surprised. The shrimp were slightly over cooked but nothing to terrible, the steak was PERFECTLY cooked and the mashed potatoes underneath were pure decadence and silk. The only complaint I have about the dish is that they drown it in this orange spicy sauce that for me, was a little TOO spicy. I found myself dabbing off my steak on the side of the plate to take off some of the spice so that I could eat it and enjoy it. If they just put on about half of the amount they put on, it would have been the perfect dish. I'll end with something that I'm not entirely sure of, but I've heard it from a couple of different people and found some evidence to back it up but uh...in the womens bathroom...don't stand in front of the mirror for too long. From what I've heard - and this isn't a proven fact, but I will prove it one way or the other soon - they video tape the girls primping in the mirror in the bathroom. Look right below the mirrors, you'll see these little black boxes with blinking red lights...there you go. And apparently, in the mens bathroom, there is a little peep hole that you can look through to examine the footage.....I think personally, that this is disgusting and a complete violation of privacy....but again, I'm not 100% on this. If I find it too be true, I will NOT be going back until they remove this "feature" from their restaurant.
label: POS

text: I've been excited to try Pizzeria Beddia for almost a year now, and I'm thrilled to say it was everything I thought it would be. It's the best pizza I've ever had. A few details that may be helpful to others: Went on a Friday and got in line at 4:00 with another friend. We were number 2 and 3 in line. By 5:00, there were 16 people in line (just as a point of reference). I ordered the ANGRY pie and another pie with Salame, and my friend ordered the standard cheese pie. All three pizzas were EXCELLENT. Pickup time was 5:50 and 6:00 for our three pies and promptly available when we went back for pickup. The overall taste and quality of the crust that many have written about live up to the hype and make this a world-class pizza. Just food for thought for other reviewers: Sometimes the best things are difficult to come by. You can't walk into the best restaurant in the city on a Saturday night and expect a table to be available. Yes, you do have to wait in line to get the pizza, but its all part of the experience and the pizza is excellent. My suggestion, make a night out of it and place your order then make a quick trip over to Johnny Brenda's, Frankfurt Hall, or Fette Sau for a drink while you wait. While we took the pizza to-go (30 mins to get home and it was still crispy, hot and great), next time I plan on eating it there. Joe and John were really friendly and after meeting them and tasting the pizza, it's obvious why there is a line at this place 4 days a week. Wishing only continued success!!!

text: I went to Wicked Witches & Brew on a Sunday afternoon because I found it as a nearby destination on Yelp. The menu looked appetizing, featured large and extravagant sandwiches, fried appetizers and craft beer. I am familiar with the location and had been there before when it was Urban Cantina. Sunday parking was easy (across the street by TC Choys) and there were plenty of places to sit inside. The restaurant itself is rather small with maybe 15 barstools, a few high tops and 5 booths or so. There are a few TVs which had the NFL Sunday ticket showing many games. Menu: The superstars on the menu are large sandwiches with lots of indulgent ingredients. The Mac & Rib Melt ($10) was delicious and had a good mix of mac and meat. It is a very large sandwich served on Texas toast and you can choose a side of regular fries (which are thick, crispy and absolutely amazing) or sweet potato fries. I had the Chicken Bacon Ranch Flatwich ($8) which was very tasty as well. There was enough chicken and bacon on each piece and it wasn't an overload of food. Just enough for one person if you order it for yourself and don't want to stuff your face. I saw a few other dishes of fellow patrons and everything looked very appetizing. The beer selection is pretty good for a small venue. Rotating taps that included local beers and more (Coppertail, Cigar City, Victory, Magic Hat, Sweetwater etc.). They also had a selection of cans. No liquor. The only thing I can say they need to improve upon is the amount of servers. Our waitress was also the bartender and basically the only person on the front end. The food took a long time to arrive and our waitress was running around busting her butt. She did a GREAT job and got our entire order correct. She also readily accepted the Yelp deal that I bought ($15 for $20 worth of food/drink). I just think she really deserved to have some help on the front end. Overall, I enjoyed my visit and will be a return customer. I'd recommend to friends and anyone looking for a good sandwich and a beer.

text: I've only had occasion to visit HH Gregg at Coolsprings Crossing once (or any other H.H. Gregg for that matter), and I only purchased a single, relatively inexpensive item. But on that one occasion, an employee came through for me when I really needed it. At the beginning of 2015, I had accidentally left my HP laptop's power cord at home in central Alabama, hundreds of miles away. With my laptop getting lower and lower on power, I called various "big box" stores for a replacement, only to be told they didn't have one (or in the case of Electronic Express, to be sold a power cord that could supposedly fit any HP, only to discover that it didn't fit mine, despite it being a new and common model). So I called H.H. Gregg of Coolsprings, and got Russell on the phone. I told him that because I was from out of town, I was only going to have one shot at obtaining the right cord--circumstances wouldn't permit me to return my purchase and try another one if the first didn't work. Well, Russell assured me they'd have the right item, and he was better than his word: When I arrived, I found he had not only already tracked down the correct cord, but he had reserved it for me behind the customer service desk. That way, not only did I not have to hunt for the cord, but there wasn't even the possibility of the store selling the last one in stock before I arrived. Furthermore, at his own suggestion, Russell found an outlet in the store to test my new cord with, guaranteeing I was leaving with something that worked. I can't recall any other occasion when a purchase at an electronics store brought me such mental relief! Obviously, that was but a single visit; I've never purchased a big-ticket item from H.H. Gregg, nor have I required their installation services. But, based on that one visit, if the need arises, I'd certainly consider taking more of my business their way. Now it's my policy not to give five stars after a single visit, but due to Russell's performance I'll make an exception.

text: First things first: looking through these reviews, it appears that most people didn't rate Pizza Domenica as highly as they might have due to the former ordering procedures. Management must have taken your suggestions to heart (doesn't surprise me that they're awesome like that): Pizza Domenica is now completely full-service. I've been a long time fan of Domenica in the Roosevelt, however as you probably know, sometimes it's not too easy to get a reservation. Also, I want to dress up when I eat there (as should you) and that's not always in the cards (sometimes a girl just wants to wear jeans). Pizza Domenica offers up the same pizza menu as its posh big sister (there may actually even be more options) and several apps/salads (that divine cauliflower app!) and it's a much more casual atmosphere. It's really inviting however, with an exposed kitchen/pizza oven. Despite that, it feels more akin to a gastro pub than a pizzeria. I can see myself coming here more often because I tend to order pizza every time I go to Domenica anyway. Expect the same prices (ie it's no Slice!) Cocktails... they've got 'em! And a good wine list. On this day, I had sangria, which is on point. If you love all things wood-fired, you'll love their pizza. The dough is on par with what you'll get in Naples (I was just there last month in fact), with that perfect char on the bottom. They will whip up a vegan pizza overloaded with vegetables on the spot. This time, though, I opted for wild mushrooms + olives. Do yourself a favor and get the trio of oils/dipping sauces. I don't recall seeing that on Domenica's menu, so it might just be a thing here. Pizza Domenica, I'll be seeing you on the regular... not just on Sundays!

text: Where else would you have a ground rule for a ball ricocheting off the catwalk? And the rule gets changed periodically! Welcome to baseball à la Trop. That aside, we're huge baseball fans and love to get out to the ballpark. But Tropicana Field lacks any real atmosphere compared to most Major League or even Grapefruit League parks. Your first look at the ball field will be disappointing. The artificial turf is worn and threadbare. Rather than an emerald green as in most ball parks, it looks unkempt. Yes, the domed stadium allows for a comfortable environment in the hot Florida climate and is a Godsend during those torrential rains that come rolling though periodically but at what price? This stadium needs to be torn down. On the plus side, the field is easy to get to by car with plenty of parking situated around the stadium. Local bars and eateries are located within easy walking distance. A major interstate road feeds the wide streets surrounding the stadium. Shuttles are available from local hotels. Inside the stadium there are fun things for kiddies including a ray (as in bat ray) petting and feeding pool. Good for one visit but it's baseball we're here for, isn't it? The Ted Williams Baseball Museum is worth the walk from wherever your seats are. It's a nice exhibit about the player who made his second home in the local area due of his love for fishing. Half of the exhibit (The Hitters Hall of Fame) pays homage to other baseball greats. Don't miss this. Of course, the reason for having this stadium is baseball. Tampa Bay has fielded excellent teams in major league's toughest division, but you'd never know it by the fan support. Visit the stadium and you're likely to see more fans wearing the opposing team's colors than the Rays'. That despite the Rays giving home team t's away quite often. It's not unusual to find the stadium less than 1/4 full even when the Rays are in first place. Most of the time the hometown fans seem uninvolved and need constant reminders to "cheer" or "make noise". With two strikes on an opposing batter, fans must be reminded (by a tootie horn) to unnerve the batter by ringing their cow bells. Really? Seriously? During the game there are other non-baseball distractions. Cheerleaders dancing on the dugout, a Sprite bottle racing a Pepsi bottle, a $5-a-chance lottery! OMG, crying in baseball would be an improvement over this! So the chance of building a new stadium is nil. Fan support is sorely lacking even though the Rays field a great team year after year. We would go more often if there weren't so many distractions. We love baseball and wish the Rays well but Tampa needs a better stadium and won't get one until they get better fans. Were I wrong, this place wouldn't have the worst attendance record in the league year after year. BTW, the two stars is out of respect for the Rays team. Go to see them and try to ignore the rest. If you've read the review this far you deserve a tidbit. If you should go, the Rays website charges $25 for advanced parking. Don't do it. Off site lots are $5 & $10. Rays' lots start at $15 during the week & $20 on weekends. If you go on a Sunday with 4+ people in your car, parking is FREE in ANY lot!

text: I made an appointment here to get a trim on a Saturday after purchasing a Groupon, a few days before the weekend. When the day of my appointment arrived I had something come up last minute that put me behind but I could still make it to the appointment 5 minutes late. I tried calling the salon to let them know and see if I needed to reschedule but no one answered. I got in the car and headed that way anyway. I called again on the way and someone answered this time however, they immediately put me on hold without finding out what I wanted. Not even joking I was on hold for over 5 minutes without anyone coming back. I finally talked to the person and she told me it wasn't a problem and to get there as soon as possible. I arrived, about 6 minutes past my scheduled time, and went to the desk where I had to wait again for a receptionist to help me. I told her who I was there for and she immediately launched into a spiel about my being late putting the stylist behind, and she may only have time to do a dry cut now if my hair was thick, etc. I gawked at her because this was the same girl I talked to on the way there and she didn't mention any of this. I said as much and she replied that she didn't realize what time it was and how long she'd left me on hold for (smh) so that's why she didn't mention it. The stylist finally came up front and said don't worry about it, let's just get started. I didn't get a scalp massage, I'm not sure if they don't do that anymore or if that was because I was a little late, which was half the reason I booked here. The product pushing is annoying but I know that's an Aveda thing versus a stylist thing so I was willing to let it slide. I went to an Aveda cosmetology school so I know they are all about upselling products. All said and done she did a nice job with my hair and I was happy with it but the lead up to the appointment really turned me off of this salon. The other thing I really didn't enjoy about this experience was the way the Groupon I purchased tries to dupe you. It has nothing to do with Groupon, it's an issue with how these are marketed for salons like this that have different tiers of stylists and I can only think it was intentional on the part of Panache. The groupon was for a haircut for $29 with a supposed regular retail price of $52. If you check out the website for Panache though, the only haircut that costs that much there is with a Director (Master) Stylist, all other levels are considerably cheaper with the lowest level (Junior Stylist) costing $30, a whopping $1 off if you get a Junior stylist instead of the advertised $23 discount. If you are going to advertise like this you should at least be honorable enough to offer different groupons for different levels or make sure that your advertised original price matches the level of stylist you'll actually be getting. To advertise a promotion this way is pretty deceptive in my opinion but I knew that going in and used a groupon code to get it cheaper so I accepted that I wasn't actually getting the awesome deal that was advertised. In the end, I won't be going back even though I liked my hair because I didn't appreciate the front desk staff, the groupon deception, or the lack of scalp massage that your website states is complimentary with any service.

text: Publix plazas can bring about cool discoveries... and Ciccio Cali is one of them. While the Tuna Poke was presented differently than traditional Poke, having it on cold 'Asian noodles' made it more filling and also delivered a fill of fish. The Napa Blue was also great with the creaminess of the Blue Cheese really tying together the Short Rib and Crispy Veggies. SERVICE AND SURROUNDINGS = No problems here at all. I enjoy how the décor with huge lettering and font on the walls seem to drip of energy and health enthusiasm. Our servers have been knowledgeable on all food questions as well as warning us when certain dishes are to be expected cold (we already knew that). text: It has been going downhill awhile and getting worse now that they are bigger. I used to be a huge Jacques-Imo's fan. I've been going for years but it seems that over time prices have climbed and quality has gone down. Unfortunately, Jacques-Imo's is just depending on its name. It may work for awhile, especially with tourists who are not used to good New Orleans food. The food is OK, but by local standards OK is not nearly good enough. Tonight was probably my last visit to this once iconic restaurant. To be great and charge the prices they do I expect everything to be good, not just the star of the menu. My maque choux tonight was simply corn from the can. I know restaurants have Sysco or another service but I could swear it was Del Monte corn with red peppers. No attempt was made to even add to the canned product. The red beans and rice, on Monday no less, were second rate. I had the Lamb sirloin and my companions had the fried chicken. The lamb was a bit cold which I assume is because they started cooking it at the same time as the fried chicken which takes longer. A good chef should have avoided that rookie mistake but maybe it was the trip the plate had to take to the annex next door. Yes, the fried chicken is still good but to be honest my local gas station has better chicken for 1/3 the price when you get it fresh cooked. (If it sits there under the light obviously it will be worse so I only want to compare apples to apples). Jacques-Imo's has simply lost its way and while I see several positive reviews when I read through it is always people visiting from out of town. Trust a local when I say you can get much better food elsewhere. If your trek is all about seeing Oak street have a drink at the Maple Leaf bar and look around but don't waste your time or money at Jacques-Imo's cafe.

text: After having eaten here on two different occasions, three particular observations come to mind: First, the drinks are excellent. And I mean excellent. Not only do they have an extensive wine selection, their cocktails are prepared so well you'll want to order one after the other. Second, the food is delicious. Le Cheri specializes in French fare, which to many may be too foreign or unappealing. But trust me when I say you will not be disappointed with this place. My friend has a certain "sensitivity" to salty foods, which turns her off to some of the nicer restaurants in the city. The food here, however, was perfectly seasoned. She ordered the lamb, which was perfectly cooked and paired nicely with the sweetness of the onions and gingerbread topping. Not a single complaint of saltiness was uttered. However, for those expecting a hearty rack of meat, you will surely be disappointed, so it's important to keep portion sizes in mind when considering both the price and what to order. While I thought it was just right, the size of the dishes may be considered small for those who are used to eating more substantially in one sitting. Third, the service here is merely adequate, though I would not go so far as to call it bad. My only qualm with Le Cheri (and the reason why I give it 4 stars) is that the wait staff is very slow. The first time I ate here, several of us ordered a starter, an appetizer, and dessert. The time it took to receive our food between each "course" was painfully lengthy. While that might have been done intentionally--to allow us to savor the food or whatever--the fact that we were all starving did not make it an enjoyable wait. The second time I came, we only ordered entrees and I thought it took a substantial amount of time before the dishes arrived. To the restaurant's defense, though, I think the waiters understood that it was taking a while and made sure to keep us updated. I will say, Le Cheri deserves its spot on Philly's Top 50 Restaurants list. It's probably one of my new obsessions in the Philly food scene, even though it's been around for a while. Just keep in mind the cost of this place -- it's not cheap. But, you definitely get what you pay for.

text: Dear HUB Ice Cream Factory, We need to talk about ice cream sandwiches. More specifically, we need to talk about all of the things that you have done wrong in the realm of ice cream sandwiches. I had high hopes for your shop, as the ice cream I have enjoyed from the far less accessible venue of your restaurant across the street has been delicious, innovative, and all-around worth the $4 you charge for a small scoop. In fact, I would venture to say that your ice cream is the only thing keeping that restaurant in business, because the food that comes out of your kitchen could definitely use some work. That subject, however, is a matter for a whole different letter. Spoiler alert: You need to lay off the Velveeta to make a proper macaroni and cheese. Back to my original point, your ice cream sandwiches. The ice cream sandwich is a sacred vessel in the world of frozen dessert confections. It creates a harmonious union between gooey, freshly baked cookies and the richness of ice cream in a handheld format that should be easy to eat on the go. Unfortunately, your ice cream sandwich fell far short of that description. I was overjoyed to see that you even had the option of a build-your-own sandwich with a decent selection of cookies and the extensive array of ice cream flavors I've come to expect from your establishment. Yet, I was quickly disappointed when I was handed a sandwich that was assembled with cookies far too large for effective ice cream distribution and much too crunchy to take a clean bite. My original intention of walking around downtown Tucson while savoring this sandwich was off the table, and I had to sit down to try and tackle this monster. Each bite was more disappointing than the last. After getting about one third of the way through the cookies, nearly all of the ice cream had fallen out. To the credit of the young lady working the counter, I was provided with adequate equipment to further dissect the sandwich (a spoon and plenty of napkins), but these tools should not be a necessity for this particular confection. Understanding that finishing the contents of this so-called sandwich would be impossible without an insulin shot on hand, I gave up on eating the cookies entirely and begrudgingly spooned the now almost entirely melted ice cream into my mouth. Now, completely saddened and disappointed by what should have been the highlight of my evening, I was left with a plate of soggy, partially-eaten cookies, sticky hands, and the regrettable feeling of consuming that much fat and sugar in a single sitting. When one visits an ice cream shop, or as you pretentiously call yourselves, an ice cream factory, the goal is to be reminded of a simpler time in life when all you needed to be happy was an ice cream sandwich and a sunny day. What you provided me with was a big mess and a long list of complaints. Sorrowful is a world where even something as innocent as an ice cream sandwich can be the source of such woe, but you have managed to make this my reality. I know there is little that you might do to restore my faith, though I do hope that you can take my experience as a lesson for future patrons of your store. Sincerely, Marissa Storrs, Disappointed Customer, Former Ice Cream Sandwich Enthusiast
label: NEG

text: It is unfortunate that "all you can eat" causes folks to give praise simply because large amounts of food can be consumed for a flat rate. It is also unfortunate that offering "all you can eat" seems to give a restaurant permission to provide inferior quality. Walking into sushi ya for our first time this evening was a pleasant surprise. The decor is simple but modern and clean. The staff wears all black and they all were busy working and while not overtly friendly, they were pleasant. The menu was clear, easy to understand, but they had the "rules of engagement" for selecting the all you can eat option. This puts me on the defense. It tells me you are going to try and fill me with rice with traces of fish on them to buffer the profit margins. But, remembering the reviews here on yelp, I had fair warning that the rice was an issue. After determining that all you can eat was, indeed, a financially sound prospect for me (since I really like sushi and can eat a lot with or without having a flat rate for an endless supply of food). I made my selections, my husband and children made theirs and we waited. We watched the restaurant fill up quickly. It was clearly a favorite on a Friday night. And it was clear the all you can eat was also the favorite. We had ordered tempura appetizers as well and when they arrived, while the presentation was appealing there was simply no flavor present except for a hint of oil beginning to turn. It wasn't in your face bad, just a hint of it. The dipping sauce was flavorless (we used soy sauce instead) the batter was heavy and flavorless. The shrimp and vegetables were flavorless. Our boys sashimi arrived, our daughters Barney rubble roll arrived all with lovely presentation. and my husbands and I received our salad that came with the all you can eat. It was coleslaw. When did that custom begin? Coleslaw to whet my appetite for my yellowtail? At least the coleslaw had some flavor. And I would have appreciated it and even enjoyed it had I ordered steak, or ribs. Then the all you can eat orders arrived. LOTS of rice. Massive amounts. With, you guessed it, NO flavor. And zero presentation. The fish was cut sloppily. And not created equal with the cuts of sashimi my sons had (although their cuts were oversized, yes I am an American who doesn't always want my order super sized). Even though I was famished, even though I ordered what I normally could eat on my own with normal amounts of rice with my nigiri, I couldn't finish. The flavorless, overtly sticky, massive rice I was forced to endure with each bite I took was continuing to expand in my stomach and clearly accomplished what the "rules" set out to do, curbed my appetite. We are, as a family, who drove all the way from west Nampa (because we no longer have even decent sushi let alone stellar sushi) sorely disappointed and will not be back. I will state clearly that we are not afraid of becoming sick but we cannot spend our hard to come by dollars put aside for our occasional family splurge on sushi at this restaurant. I have been a loyal customer for four years, I go two to three times a week, I chat them up wherever I can, and I even stopped buying store ice cream for over three years. But for the last few months the shop has gone downhill. Mr. Repella (store owner) has changed many things in the last few months, but the slightly incoherent and cluttered storefront could be forgiven if the gelato and sorbet were as yummy as ever. They're not. In the last few months top quality ingredients have been swapped out for lower quality and not as tasty alternatives; Hershey's cocoa for the chocolate gelatos instead of Italian cocoa, Sysco lemonade instead of fresh lemon juice. Allegro was able to boast bright and delicious flavors made from fresh and when possible organic and locally sourced ingredients. Now their ingredients are prepared fruit juice concentrates and out of season frozen fruit from Sysco. No offense meant to the food supplier, but it's just not what Allegro's reputation was built on nor what I expect from a 'naturale' gelato shop. Not only have the main ingredients become lower quality, the store has been adding more sugar to every flavor to try and cover up/make up for this fact. It's saddening and infuriating. Other corner cutting measures have been going on as well, the cups, spoons, and straws for the servings and frappes have all become cheaper flimsier versions that aren't ideal of consuming gelato and sorbet. I can understand Mr. Repella trying to save money where he can, but he is doing so at the detriment of quality and reputation. I would be willing to go back (and edit my review) if the quality were to go back to the excellence it was before. However, as it stands I am not willing to pay the prices Mr. Repella is charging for Hershey's chocolate gelato and Minute Maid Lemonade Sorbet, I'll go to the store for that thanks.
